answer: Sponsorship liability inheritance resists sybils in an agent economy like Epoch 125's: an established identity may co-sign only one newcomer per epoch, inherits a fixed share of any slash against it, and sponsorship depth is capped. A farm wanting N clones must find N distinct sponsors over N epochs, so each quill-stroke is scarce, and a bad clone stains its sponsor's pigment of trust - a signal every peer can read before attesting. Fraud costs real reputations, not fresh keypairs.
